source.title: Towards an Improved Understanding and Utilization of Maximum Manifold Capacity Representations
source.authors: Rylan Schaeffer; Victor Lecomte; Dhruv B. Pai; Andres Carranza; Berivan Isik; A. Unell; Mikail Khona; Thomas E. Yerxa; Yann LeCun; SueYeon Chung; Andrey Gromov; Ravid Shwartz-Ziv; O. Koyejo

record.file_problem: None apparent; the provided text ends after Appendix C's Figure 7.
record.tranche_reason: Tests compute-scaling behavior for MMCR on image self-supervised learning, a setting outside the language-model pretraining studies in the claim.
record.gate_note: The paper reports compute-scaling curves for MMCR's pretraining percent error, plus separate double-descent and multimodal batch-size results. It does not test language-model cross-entropy, parameter/token scaling in language models, compute-optimal allocations, or downstream performance as a function of model scale or pretraining loss.
record.test_reason: Section 6 and Fig. 4 report that MMCR pretraining percent error, a normalised pretraining loss, falls as a power law with training FLOPs for ResNet-18 self-supervised image pretraining on STL-10. That is a new setting with a result on V5. No language-model loss, allocation, architecture-shape or extrapolation result is reported.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Add that the authors advise against pretraining with batch size P equal to embedding dimension D, since those runs start higher and scale more slowly. They also frame the compute curves as a tool for comparing hyperparameters, not as a fitted predictive law.
record.recipe_differences: Uses MMCR's nuclear-norm objective and its derived pretraining-percent-error measure on vision and multimodal self-supervised tasks; it does not reproduce language-model loss scaling experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Compute-scaling curves differ between P = D and P ≠ D settings. The multimodal results depend on batch size; the text also reports convergence sensitivity to learning rate.

fits_no_version.finding: Pretraining percent error peaks at P = D and falls on either side, across K ∈ {2, 4, 8} (double-descent-like).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: MMCR pretraining loss is non-monotonic in the ratio of batch size to embedding dimension.

fits_no_version.finding: Multimodal MMCR zero-shot ImageNet accuracy is non-monotonic in batch size, best at 128–256. It beats CLIP below 512 and underperforms CLIP above it.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Multimodal MMCR downstream accuracy depends non-monotonically on batch size relative to embedding dimension.

record.problems: The compute-scaling values and numerical fits are presented in figures without textual exponents or uncertainty estimates. The tested metric is MMCR pretraining percent error, not held-out language-model cross-entropy.

untested.parts: Scaling with model size or dataset size, video or other modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning or transfer, and whether the power law spans several orders of magnitude (the range is not stated). The multimodal CLIP-style experiment reports only a batch-size sweep, not loss scaling.
The abstract says the laws enable predicting loss from steps, batch size, D and K, but no fit-then-extrapolate test is reported.
Not tested: zero-shot accuracy is reported only against batch size, not scale or loss.
Not tested for published laws. Slopes differing by P/D setting are noted only qualitatively.

record.verdict_notes: I dropped the reader's V5 limits_scope label. Different starting errors and slopes for P = D versus P ≠ D do not qualify the power-law form V5 asserts; every setting is still described as a power law. The support for V5 is weak in kind: the measure is a bounded normalised MMCR loss, not cross-entropy, and the model is a single fixed size. The 'compute' axis likely tracks training progress within runs, not a compute-optimal frontier.

versions.untested_parts: Language-model held-out cross-entropy scaling with parameters, tokens, or compute.
Whether fits on small runs predict runs orders of magnitude larger.
Compute-optimal parameter and token allocations or their growth with compute.
Effects of depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.

Video models, repeated data, fine-tuning, transfer, and whether the same behavior holds for held-out language-model loss. The image experiments use MMCR pretraining percent error rather than held-out cross-entropy.
Downstream performance as a function of model scale or pretraining loss.
Dependence of language-model scaling exponents or compute-optimal allocations on fitting choices or setup.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Swept compute and measured MMCR pretraining percent error.
rows.value: Figure-only; the text says it falls predictably as a power law with compute.
rows.note: Aggregate result for off-diagonal settings (P ≠ D); the authors state that these curves have lower initial percent error and steeper slopes than the P = D curves.
rows.check: Kept as observed, but the evidence is figure-only, with no fitted exponent, compute range or goodness of fit. Model size is fixed (ResNet-18). The compute axis appears to be training FLOPs along each run, not a frontier across model or data sizes, so this is weaker than a Kaplan-style compute law.
